articles.title: How to Structure Engineering Teams as You Scale: A Team Topologies Guide for Leaders
articles.excerpt: Short answer Structure engineering around the flow of business value. Most engineers should sit in small, long-lived stream-aligned teams that own a product area end to end. Add a platform team when t…
articles.body: Short answer Structure engineering around the flow of business value. Most engineers should sit in small, long-lived stream-aligned teams that own a product area end to end. Add a platform team when teams repeat the same infrastructure work, enabling teams to spread new skills, and a complicated-subsystem team only for deep specialist parts. Keep each team’s cognitive load manageable. 4 - team types: stream-aligned, platform, enabling, complicated subsystem 3 - ways teams interact: collaboration, X-as-a-Service, facilitation 5–9 - people per team, a common size for shared context and ownership 1 - clear owner for every service, incident and roadmap The best way to structure engineering teams as you scale is around the flow of business value, not around technologies or job titles.

articles.title: Tracking GENIUS Act rulemaking with the Federal Register API (and why a naive search lies to you)
articles.excerpt: The US stablecoin law, the GENIUS Act, was signed on 18 July 2025. Since then the federal banking agencies and Treasury have been publishing proposed rules, notices and, now, final rules. Every one of…
articles.body: The US stablecoin law, the GENIUS Act, was signed on 18 July 2025. Since then the federal banking agencies and Treasury have been publishing proposed rules, notices and, now, final rules. Every one of them lands in the Federal Register, which has a free, keyless JSON API. This post walks through a short script that builds a clean list of those documents, and through the two traps I hit on the way: a search term that matches far too much, and a "document type" field that does not mean what you think. The endpoint GET https://www.federalregister.gov/api/v1/documents.json Useful parameters: conditions[term] for full-text search fields[] (repeatable) to choose which fields come back per_page (up to 100) and order the response's next_page_url for pagination No API key and no auth.

articles.excerpt: I type a lot less than I used to. I hold two keys, say what I want, let go, and the text shows up wherever my cursor is. Slack, VS Code, a Gmail draft, a terminal. It works with the Wi-Fi off. That ap…
articles.body: I type a lot less than I used to. I hold two keys, say what I want, let go, and the text shows up wherever my cursor is. Slack, VS Code, a Gmail draft, a terminal. It works with the Wi-Fi off. That app is Talvio . It's open source (MIT), built with Tauri 2, Rust and React, and it runs on Windows and Linux today. A macOS build is coming. GitHub: github.com/ishangautam7/Talvio This post is half "here's what I made" and half "here's what broke". If you build desktop apps with Tauri, the second half is probably the useful part. Why I built it I wanted dictation that worked in every app, not just in one website's text box. I also didn't want my voice going to a server every time I wrote a Slack message. I found Handy by CJ Pais.

articles.title: Serving Markdown to AI agents from a Cloudflare Worker, without a second copy of the site
articles.excerpt: AI agents read web pages the expensive way. They download the HTML, throw away the navigation, scripts and styles, and try to recover the text. Some of them now send Accept: text/markdown and take Mar…
articles.body: AI agents read web pages the expensive way. They download the HTML, throw away the navigation, scripts and styles, and try to recover the text. Some of them now send Accept: text/markdown and take Markdown if the server offers it. I wanted our landing page to answer that request without keeping a second Markdown copy of the site in sync by hand. The site is static files behind a Cloudflare Worker, so the Worker converts the HTML on the way out. This post walks through that module: about 160 lines, no dependencies, built on HTMLRewriter . Step 1: decide when to convert The rule is narrow on purpose.

articles.title: Developer-friendly automated security feedback in pull requests
articles.excerpt: Contents Make security feedback non-blocking but unignorable Design PR gates and SAST hooks that respect developer flow Cut noise with filters, thresholds, and clear policy Automate triage and coach d…
articles.body: Contents Make security feedback non-blocking but unignorable Design PR gates and SAST hooks that respect developer flow Cut noise with filters, thresholds, and clear policy Automate triage and coach developers inside the PR A deployable checklist to roll this into your CI The problem you live with is predictable: noisy SAST results land in PRs or tickets, reviewers spend time triaging false positives, and developers bypass checks or defer fixes until a later sprint. That deferral accumulates security debt , makes remediation more expensive, and pushes detection farther from authoring — outcomes that escalate risk and cost for the business. The point here is not theoretical: long detection-to-fix windows correlate with higher breach impact and cost.

articles.title: Open-source LLM apps, from fine-tuning to group chat: 8 notes on Oumi, F5-TTS, VideoLingo, LangBot and more
articles.excerpt: Most of the interesting open-source LLM work right now isn't a new model. It's the plumbing around models: the pipelines that fine-tune them, the bots that put them in a group chat, the tools that tur…
articles.body: Most of the interesting open-source LLM work right now isn't a new model. It's the plumbing around models: the pipelines that fine-tune them, the bots that put them in a group chat, the tools that turn a video into subtitles in another language. I went back through my bookmarked notes on that layer and pulled out eight projects that, between them, cover most of the path from training a model to putting it in front of people. My view after rereading them: the hard part has moved from "can a model do this" to "who owns the glue," and the projects below are where that glue is being written in the open. Training and evaluating Oumi. If you want one toolchain for data prep, fine-tuning, evaluation and serving, Oumi is the most complete open option I've saved.

articles.title: Analog astronauts: How living underwater can prepare humans for space missions
articles.excerpt: How living underwater can prepare humans for space missions
articles.body: I have been dreaming of doing research in space as an astronaut my whole life, but for some reason, the thought of working underwater made me nervous. I’ve known for a long time that astronauts train underwater to simulate different scenarios they’re likely to experience in space. Diving was never an issue for me, either — I even made it as far as becoming a certified rescue diver. So what was the problem? This summer, I led a simulated space mission in an underwater habitat called the Jules’ Undersea Lab. It is a research station that is located 22 feet (6.7 meters) underwater near Key Largo, Florida. You have to scuba dive to get in and out of the station. To become an aquanaut , you have to stay underwater for at least 24 hours in a so-called state of saturation.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 26, 2004: Cassini spacecraft takes 1st-ever closeup photos of Saturn moon Titan
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 26, 2004, NASA's Cassini spacecraft took the first close-up images of Saturn's largest moon Titan. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 26, 2004, NASA's Cassini spacecraft took the first close-up images of Saturn's largest moon Titan. The Cassini spacecraft would later drop off a probe on Titan named Huygens, which was a European spacecraft that hitched a ride to the Saturn system with the Cassini mission. But before Cassini dropped off its robotic passenger, it flew by Titan a few times and took some amazing photos . Cassini completed its first flyby on July 3, 2004, but when it swung by a second time on Oct. 26, it got about 300 times closer than it did the first time. At the closest point of this flyby, Cassini was 745 miles (1,200 kilometers) away from the surface of Titan. The spacecraft took hundreds of photos during this flyby , and these were the highest resolution views of Titan anyone had ever seen.

articles.title: NASA ends Swift space telescope mission after failed rescue attempt
articles.excerpt: NASA has officially ended the mission of its Swift Observatory, after a private satellite failed to meet up with the aging spacecraft in orbit.
articles.body: NASA has officially ended the mission of its Swift space telescope, after a private satellite failed in its bold bid to rescue the aging spacecraft. That rescue mission was led by the Arizona company Katalyst Space Technologies, whose LINK spacecraft tried to meet up with Swift this summer to boost its orbit. That didn't work out, however, so Swift continues its fall back toward Earth. The telescope is expected to reenter Earth's atmosphere "in the next few weeks," NASA said in a statement on Friday (Oct. 23). That statement served primarily to announce the end of the Swift mission after more than 20 very productive years. The telescope launched to Earth orbit in November 2004, tasked with studying gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) — the most powerful explosions in the cosmos.
